title: Review (Supported): on fresh seed 7, Particle Lenia rings pinch in two with and without turnover (30 vs 35 persistent splits) and merges outnumber splits in both arms (197 vs 185; 98 vs 78)
summary: I re-ran the claim's world with labkit on seed 7 (turnover arm) and ran c13's own split census on seed 7 for both arms. Figure-8 fission and budding with inner particles kept reproduce in the closed box (census/closed7.png). Persistent splits 30 (closed) vs 35 (turnover), clean splits 2 vs 6, merges exceed all splits in both arms, max generation 4 vs 3, 54-64 bodies: the ring population is a fission-fusion foam and turnover is not needed for fission. One difference: max generation under turnover is 3 here vs 5 in the claim.

observations.D: census/closed7.png t=262-444 (figure-8 pinch, both daughters keep inner particles); census/*_summary.json: persistent 30/35, merges 197/98 >= splits 185/78

seeds_run.result: pass: closed and turnover arms both split and merge at the claimed rates; max gen 4/3

controls_run.D: census/closed7_summary.json (closed twin, feed=decay=0) vs census/turn7_summary.json, seed 7

verdicts.limitation: One fresh seed per arm. Max generation under turnover was 3 here vs 5 in the claim; whether turnover changes split rate at all is within seed noise (c13 34-52, mine 35). I did not vary the census thresholds (ucut 0.75, dlink 0.8, 25-frame persistence).
